description.text: Hormel Foods Corporation, a Delaware corporation, was founded by George A. Hormel in 1891 in Austin, Minnesota, as Geo. A. Hormel & Company. The Company originated as a processor of meat and food products and continues in this line of business today. The Company has expanded its product portfolio through organic growth and acquisitions to become a global branded food company with more than $12 billion in annual revenue. The Company is built on a foundation of innovation and integrity and a commitment to delivering high-quality, trusted food products across a diverse portfolio of brands and product solutions including Planters®, SPAM®, Jennie-O®, Skippy®, Applegate®, Wholly®, Hormel® Black Label®, Fontanini®, Bacon1®, Hormel® pepperoni, and more than 30 other beloved brands. The Company is a member of the S&P 500 Index and the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats. When used in this report, the terms "we," "our," "us," and the "Company" mean Hormel Foods Corporation and its subsidiaries, collectively, unless the context otherwise requires or indicates.

about.description_short: Hormel Foods Corporation, based in Austin, Minnesota, is a global branded food company with over $12 billion in annual revenue. Its brands include PLANTERS, SKIPPY, SPAM, HORMEL NATURAL CHOICE, APPLEGATE, WHOLLY, HORMEL BLACK LABEL, COLUMBUS, JENNIE-O and more than 30 other beloved brands. The Company is a member of the S&P 500 Index and the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats, was named one of the best companies to work for by U.S. News & World Report and one of America's most responsible companies by Newsweek, was recognized by TIME magazine as one of the World's Best Companies and has received numerous other awards and accolades for its corporate responsibility and community service efforts.

analysis_md:
# HRL — Hormel Foods Corporation
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-19. Engine release 5.4.0. Price $20.28 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $11.164B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Austin, Minnesota branded protein foods company (SIC 2011, meat packing): SPAM, Skippy peanut butter, Planters snack nuts, Jennie-O turkey, Applegate natural/organic meats, Columbus charcuterie, Hormel chili and pepperoni. Three segments — Retail, Foodservice, International. A Dividend King: the fiscal 2025 release noted a 1% quarterly dividend increase marking 60 years of uninterrupted dividend growth. Portfolio is being reshaped: the whole-bird turkey business was slated for sale to Life-Science Innovations, the Brazil operation (Ceratti) was sold / classified held for sale in fiscal 2026, and on 2026-09-30 the company agreed to acquire chicken processor Brakebush Brothers for $1.055B (expected close Q1 FY2027, funded with cash and new debt, ~$1.2B of trailing sales, accretive to adjusted EPS only from FY2028).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K, period ended 2025-10-26, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $845,251,000; capex $310,902,000 (tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, filed every year — no gap, no override); SBC $25,602,000 (always a real cost, though small here at ~3% of OCF).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $508,747,000 = $0.92/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $0.92, latest FY OE total $508.7M) — a depressed year: commodity cost inflation (pork bellies, beef, nuts) squeezed cash margins and OCF fell from the prior year's level even though the $234M non-cash impairment (below) is added back inside OCF.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $229,312,000 per the filed history — below the conservative figure, mainly a working-capital artifact of the same weak year; the OCF-based conservative series is the one used throughout.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (key_numbers.md). Per-share OE history is volatile around a flat center: $1.37 (FY2023), $1.80 (FY2024), $0.92 (FY2025) — the 3-year median is $1.37/share.
- Balance sheet (latest FY, from dcf_numbers.json / key_numbers.md): net debt $2.187B, which is 2.90x normalized OE; lease liabilities $167,986,000 sit outside that net-debt figure. Shares diluted (latest) 550,496,000; share count is essentially flat (+0.06%/yr) — no buyback tailwind and no dilution problem.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q3 FY2026 (period ended 2026-07-26), from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $845,251,000 − prior YTD $522,345,000 + current YTD $768,752,000 = **TTM $1,091,658,000**
- Capex: FY $310,902,000 − prior YTD $219,444,000 + current YTD $219,331,000 = **TTM $310,789,000**
- SBC: FY $25,602,000 − prior YTD $21,387,000 + current YTD $21,293,000 = **TTM $25,508,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **550,898,000**
- **TTM OE total $755,361,000 → base OE/share $1.37** (base_source: ttm_json; key_numbers.md rounds it to $1.37)
- The TTM base lands exactly on the engine's normalized base (3-yr median $1.37/share): the two independent bases agree, which is the strongest evidence that FY2025's $0.92 was a trough print, not the run rate — and equally that there is no growth in the base itself. Fundamentals.json's TTM block independently shows the same TTM OE total ($755,361,000) and TTM revenue of $12,146,911,000, up only 0.73% year over year.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: genuine brands and foodservice relationships, but incomplete commodity pass-through, eroding margins, and ROIC that has fallen to around the cost of capital — no score above the moderate band is justified.
- FOR: Durable branded portfolio with real shelf presence: SPAM, Skippy, Planters, Jennie-O, Applegate, Columbus, Hormel chili and pepperoni; Foodservice channel strength — 12th consecutive quarter of organic net sales growth in Q3 FY2026, premium prepared proteins and branded pepperoni; scale in value-added protein processing and long-standing retail/foodservice relationships, with 60 consecutive years of dividend increases; pricing actions are sticking on an adjusted basis — FY2026 YTD adjusted operating margin +30bp and adjusted EPS +6% through Q3.
- AGAINST: Commodity input costs (pork bellies, beef, turkey, nuts) cannot be fully or quickly passed through — FY2025 gross margin fell to 15.6% from 17.0%; the ROIC proxy fell from 17–21% (FY2016–19) to 8–10% (FY2021–24) and 5.1% in impairment-hit FY2025 (fundamentals.json roic_proxy series), so returns no longer clear the cost of capital by a wide margin; private label and cautious consumers — Retail volume fell ~9% in Q3 FY2026 and organic net sales fell 2% in the quarter; capital-allocation scars — the $3.35B Planters acquisition (2021) was followed by Retail intangible impairments in FY2025, and International minority investments were impaired in both FY2025 and FY2026; exposure to shifting protein tastes with no structural cost advantage over larger packaged-food peers.
- Evidence (fundamentals.json): gross margin over the last five fiscal years ran 16.9% / 17.4% / 16.5% / 17.0% / 15.6% (FY2021–FY2025), down from 19.0–22.7% in FY2016–20; the roic_proxy series over the same five years ran 9.4% / 10.4% / 8.1% / 8.2% / 5.1%. A moat of 7+ requires ROIC well above the cost of capital through a cycle — Hormel no longer shows that.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
The engine's blended growth is 0.24% (components: rev CAGR 5y 4.73%, rev CAGR 3y −0.96%, latest rev YoY 1.55%, OE/share CAGR 2y −18.00%, share-count adjustment −0.06%). Sanity check against actual prints: TTM revenue grew only 0.73% YoY and Q3 FY2026 net sales fell 2.4% (organic −2%), while management cut FY2026 guidance to $12.1–12.2B of net sales (organic +1% to +2%) — but raised adjusted EPS guidance to $1.45–$1.51 (+6% to +10%) and adjusted operating income to $1.08–1.12B on margin recovery and pricing. OE growth, not revenue growth, is the recovering leg: TTM OE is already back to the 3-year median after the FY2025 trough. Scenario growth starts were therefore set with offsets −12 / −5 / +1.76 / +4.76 / +8.76pp against the blend, giving starts of −10.0% (the engine's floor binds on the super-bear offset) / −4.8% / **2.0%** / 5.0% / 9.0%: the base start sits modestly above the revenue prints because it is an OE/share start in a guided margin-recovery year, and the bull and super-bull starts (5.0% / 9.0%) are OE-recovery paths — margin normalization plus, in the super-bull case, Brakebush consolidating from FY2027 — not revenue forecasts; no scenario assumes revenue growth anywhere near its start figure. Probabilities are the defaults 10/25/30/25/10 and OE multipliers the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $20.28.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −10.0% | 0.75 | Commodity spike repeats, volumes keep falling, another impairment cycle | $4.99 | 5.14% |
| Bear | 25% | −4.8% | 0.90 | FY2025 conditions linger; guidance cut extends into FY2027 | $7.47 | 6.81% |
| Base | 30% | 2.0% | 1.00 | Flat revenue, slow margin recovery to the median OE base growing gently | $11.01 | 9.27% |
| Bull | 25% | 5.0% | 1.10 | Pricing + Transform & Modernize deliver the guided adjusted-EPS growth | $13.72 | 11.04% |
| Super bull | 10% | 9.0% | 1.25 | Full margin normalization plus Brakebush accretion from FY2028 | $18.40 | 13.91% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $10.94 (−46.0% vs price), IV@12% $14.39, IV@10% $18.22, weighted IRR 9.24%, base-case IRR 9.27%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 6.76%, terminal value 17.7% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.69x, net debt 2.90x normalized OE, 11.8 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path, key_numbers.md): clears 15% only at $10.94, 20% at $7.82, 25% at $6.09. Even the super-bull scenario's IV@15 ($18.40) sits below the $20.28 price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 12 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q3 FY2026 (period ended 2026-07-26), quoted leg by leg above, and it independently reproduces the 3-year median base ($1.37/share both ways).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025): the one-off is identified — FY2025 net income of $478,197,000 was crushed by $234M of non-cash impairment charges taken in Q4 FY2025 (primarily a minority investment in the International segment and certain intangible assets in the Retail segment, per the company's fiscal 2025 release), which are added back in operating cash flow of $845,251,000; GAAP operating income was $719M against adjusted operating income of $1,019M, and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.87 against adjusted $1.37. The divergence therefore flatters neither series: the impairment is non-cash so the OCF-based OE base is not contaminated by it — but note the pattern is repeating, with FY2026 GAAP guidance cut to $1.06–$1.12 for a Brazil divestiture loss, a further Indonesian minority-investment impairment, and a litigation settlement, while adjusted guidance was raised to $1.45–$1.51. Recurring "one-offs" are a real earnings-quality drag and a reason confidence is not high; they do not change the cash OE base.
